headline: GOLD BREAKS TO 7-WEEK LOW AT $4,148 — OIL TOPS $106 AS TRUMP REJECTS IRAN HORMUZ DEAL; FED HIKE ODDS AT 70%
snippet: Gold dropped 3.2% to $4,148 per ounce on September 28 — a seven-week low — after President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, pushing Brent crude above $106 per barrel and reigniting inflation fears that hardened Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations. The CME FedWatch October hike probability moved to 70.3% from 64.2% on Friday, the 10-year Treasury yield climbed back above 5.2%, and silver fell harder, dropping 4.3% to $61.53, breaking below the $62.30 support traders had flagged as near-term critical. The week ahead features PCE inflation data (Wednesday) and non-farm payrolls (Friday) as the two macro events most likely to force a rapid shift in rate expectations; if PCE surprises to the downside, the hike probability repricing could provide a sharp reversal in precious metals before month-end.

headline: B2GOLD TATTUK ZONE: 9.95M AT 10.94 G/T AU — NEW NUNAVUT GOLD SYSTEM FOUND 150M BEYOND KNOWN RESOURCE; GOOSE ON TRACK FOR 200KOZ
snippet: B2Gold (TSX: BTO; NYSE American: BTG) released a combined operations update and drill discovery announcement for its Goose Mine in Nunavut on September 28, revealing the new Tattuk Zone — 9.95 metres grading 10.94 g/t Au from approximately 1,196 metres depth, located about 150 metres down-plunge from the existing Nuvuyak mineral inventory. Additional results include 21.23 metres at 19.12 g/t Au at the Llama deposit and 6.9 metres at 11.88 g/t Au at Nuvuyak; operationally, the replacement mobile crushing plant commissioned after April's crusher fire has processed more than 3,000 tonnes per day since mid-August, and Goose Mine remains on track for its 2026 production guidance of 170,000–200,000 ounces. The Tattuk Zone is a new discovery footprint below the current resource that could contribute to a future resource update at the Back River Gold District, making this one of the more substantive combined operations-and-discovery releases of the September exploration season.

headline: COPPER LME DROPS 1.8% TO $14,364 — CHINA PROFIT GROWTH SLOWS TO 4.2% IN AUGUST; GOLDEN WEEK SELLING ADDS PRESSURE
snippet: LME benchmark copper fell 1.8% to $14,364 per metric tonne on September 28 as Chinese industrial enterprise profit growth slowed to 4.2% year-on-year in August — the weakest reading since late 2025 and a sharp deceleration from July's 11% rate — while Chinese market participants reduced pre-Golden Week exposure ahead of the October 1–7 holiday period. COMEX copper holds near $6.70 per pound, still within 2% of the September 22 all-time record of $6.83/lb, with the Escondida supervisors' strike vote (September 28–30) and a pending White House decision on a proposed 15–30% tariff on refined copper imports both capable of moving the market materially before the week is out. For junior copper investors, the combination of a China demand slowdown signal and seasonal selling pressure represents a healthy pullback test of the post-record structure, not a trend reversal.

headline: LUNDIN GOLD BREAKS DEPOSIT RECORD: 204.26 G/T AU OVER 3M AND 1,035 G/T BONANZA AT FRUTA DEL NORTE; QUEBRADA DORADA EXTENDS TREND TO 8 KM
snippet: Lundin Gold (TSX: LUG) reported on September 24 the highest-grade drill result in Fruta del Norte's operating history: hole BLP-2026-553 at the Bonza Sur target returned 204.26 g/t Au over 3.05 metres, including a 60-centimetre bonanza interval of 1,035.60 g/t Au — the highest grade ever recorded in a drill hole at this deposit. Simultaneously, hole CHT-2026-495 at the newly identified Quebrada Dorada vein system returned 13 metres at 6.53 g/t Au from 195 metres, extending the continuous gold epithermal trend from 5 to 8 kilometres of strike length — a 60% expansion of the known mineralized corridor. For a mine with a 12-year mine life, the combination of a record-grade result at a known target and a new 3-kilometre district extension on the same day is a rare disclosure that meaningfully improves the odds of a resource addition and life extension at one of the Americas' highest-grade operating gold mines.

headline: SELLERS CONTROL GOLD AT $4,143 — CAN MONTH-END FLOWS AND FRIDAY NFP REVERSE THE CORRECTION? PCE WEDNESDAY IS THE KEY
snippet: FXStreet's September 28 technical analysis identifies gold's breach of $4,225 support toward $4,143 and silver's break of $62.30 as the defining technical events of the weekly open, with sellers in control unless macro data forces a rapid re-pricing of Federal Reserve expectations. Month-end rebalancing flows — which historically favour gold after a month of equity outperformance — represent a potential near-term counterforce, while Wednesday's PCE inflation print and Friday's non-farm payrolls are identified as the two most likely reversal catalysts; a soft PCE reading could collapse the CME FedWatch 70% October hike probability quickly. The analysis marks $4,100–$4,157 as the next support band and notes the current 6.5% pullback from the September peak near $4,440 remains within the range of every prior correction in the 2025–2026 bull run — none of which exceeded 8% before resuming higher — distinguishing this as a normal cyclical reset rather than a structural top.

headline: UEC REPORTS FISCAL 2026 PRE-MARKET TOMORROW — FIRST FULL YEAR FROM BURKE HOLLOW; PRIOR QUARTER SOLD $101/LB AGAINST $89 SPOT
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE American: UEC) will report fiscal year 2026 results before markets open on September 29, with a conference call at 11:00 a.m. ET — the first full fiscal year that includes production data from Burke Hollow in Texas, America's largest new greenfield in-situ recovery uranium project in over a decade. In Q3 FY2026, UEC sold 200,000 pounds of U3O8 from its physical portfolio at $101 per pound against a spot price of approximately $89 per pound, generating $10 million gross profit — a premium that validates the company's strategy of holding physical inventory rather than selling at below-spot long-term contract prices. UEC enters the results week with $794 million in liquid assets and no debt; analyst consensus estimates Q4 revenue of approximately $9 million with EPS of -$0.05, though full-year Burke Hollow throughput and cost data is the disclosure most closely watched for establishing the operating economics of the US uranium production expansion cycle.

headline: RAMELIUS MAPS 610KOZ GOLD AND $2BN CASH FLOW BY FY30 — MT MAGNET MILL DOUBLES; GOLDSEEK SWOT FLAGS ASX RE-RATING POTENTIAL
snippet: GoldSeek's Gold SWOT analysis covers Ramelius Resources' (ASX: RMS) revised four-year production plan targeting 560–610 koz of annual gold output by FY30 — an 11% increase from the prior October 2025 plan — driven by a Mt Magnet mill expansion from 2.0 to 4.3–5.0 Mtpa at A$340–360 million capital cost. FY27 guidance is set at 205,000–225,000 oz at A$2,150–2,350/oz AISC; exploration success has already lifted expected mill grade from 2.9 to 3.4 g/t, adding approximately 60,000 oz (+16%) to FY30 output beyond the expansion budget's original assumption. At current gold prices above AUD $6,600/oz, the FY27 guidance generates margins the market has not fully priced into Ramelius's ASX valuation, making it a SWOT-highlighted re-rating candidate in the mid-tier ASX gold space — a segment retail investors in Australian gold miners increasingly focus on as the junior exploration sector compresses valuations for companies without near-term production milestones.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH EXPORT FREEZE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — CSIS: WESTERN SUPPLY CHAINS STILL NOT DIVERSIFIED ONE YEAR LATER
snippet: A Center for Strategic and International Studies analysis examining China's rare earth export control framework one year after its announcement finds that the 12-month suspension agreed at the October 2025 Busan APEC summit expires on November 10, 2026 — now just six weeks away — with Western rare earth separation and processing capacity still covering less than 15–20% of projected ex-China demand. China's framework applies a Foreign Direct Product Rule-style licensing requirement to any product containing 0.1% or more of Chinese-origin rare earths or manufactured using Chinese processing technology, extending regulatory reach across the entire global rare earth value chain including EV motors, wind turbine generators, and defense-grade magnets. For retail investors tracking rare earth juniors on the TSXV, ASX, and Nasdaq, the November 10 deadline is the single most important near-term policy catalyst in the sector: reimposition of controls would immediately accelerate project financing discussions for ex-China heavy rare earth developers and could add meaningful urgency premium to advanced-stage projects like Critical Metals Corp's Tanbreez (NASDAQ: CRML) and Lynas Rare Earths' (ASX: LYC) Malaysian separation facility.

headline: BRENT ABOVE $106, IRAN TALKS STALL — HOW THE HORMUZ OIL SPIKE IS HITTING MINING MARKETS ACROSS COMMODITIES
snippet: Saxo Bank's September 28 Macro Quick Take identifies the fresh surge in Brent crude above $106 per barrel — triggered by Trump's rejection of Iran's seven-day Strait of Hormuz reopening proposal, with both sides returning to negotiations this week — as the catalyst behind simultaneous weakness in precious metals, base metals, and risk assets at the start of a data-heavy macro week. For mining investors, the oil spike has two direct effects: it increases diesel and fuel costs at open-pit mining operations (typically 15–20% of cash costs), compressing margins even as gold and copper nominally trade near historic highs; and it reinforces inflation expectations that extend the period of Federal Reserve rate hikes, sustaining dollar strength and Treasury yield pressure on non-yielding assets like gold and silver. WTI crude is trading above $94 per barrel; both sides have signalled a return to Hormuz negotiations this week, meaning any progress on a deal could rapidly reverse the oil spike and remove the macro headwind from precious metals.
